r3-evidence.finding:
Criterion B reproduced independently, mutating the REAL scripts/mcp_spine_server.py each time, restoring via git checkout, confirming git diff HEAD~1 -- scripts/ back to 0 lines after each. Baseline: python -m pytest -q tests/test_mcp_identity.py::IdentityBindingPinTests -> 5 passed. Mutation 1 (add spine_file to spine_status inputSchema properties) -> RED on exactly test_no_tool_accepts_an_argument_that_could_redirect_the_door (matches Commander claim); restored -> 5 passed. Mutation 2 (SPINE late-bound via module __getattr__ instead of import-time binding) -> RED on test_identity_is_bound_at_import_and_is_immune_to_later_environment_change (matches Commander claim) PLUS a bonus RED on test_two_doors_bound_to_two_spines_do_not_share_a_binding (KeyError, since env is restored by the time that later assertion re-reads module.SPINE); restored -> 5 passed. Mutation 3 (mine): call_tool's spine_status handler honors an undeclared spine_override argument (never added to any inputSchema) that redirects the engine call to an arbitrary --file path -- a genuine per-call identity-redirect implemented purely in dispatch logic, invisible to the schema the pin inspects. Result: 5 passed, NO test went red. Restored -> 5 passed, diff clean. FINDING: IdentityBindingPinTests only inspects declared TOOLS schema shape and import-time SPINE/SESSION binding; it never exercises call_tool's actual runtime dispatch. IDENTITY_TRADE.md's claim 'the door literally cannot be pointed at another run's spine, because there is no argument that would let it... confinement by construction, not by convention' is therefore stronger than what the pin backs: a future change to call_tool alone, never touching a tool's inputSchema, defeats that claim silently.
